sop_title: NETCINST 4200.4A Enclosure (1): Government-Wide Commercial Purchase Card Program (GCPC) Internal Operating Procedures
summary: This SOP covers NETC's purchase card program from start to finish: appointing and training cardholders, obtaining funding, making micro-purchases, monthly statement reconciliation and certification, disputes, fraud, lost cards, departures, and internal and external program reviews. It is run by cardholders (CH), Approving/Certifying Officials (AO/CO), the A/OPC (GCPC Program Manager, N4), N8 funds managers, requesting departments, and CITIBANK.

risks.process: Reconcile and certify the monthly statement
risks.what_could_go_wrong: The cardholder and AO/CO plan to the 10-business-day certification deadline and miss the 5-business-day reconciliation deadline. The reverse can also happen, with each party assuming the other has more time.
risks.cause: Section 10 requires the CH and AO/CO to complete reconciliation within five business days of the status change from INTERIM to NEW. Section 10.b(6) gives the AO/CO 10 business days from the same status change to certify. The SOP does not say which deadline governs the joint process or how the 5 days split between CH and AO/CO.
risks.impact: Statements are certified late or rushed. This can lead to late payment to CITIBANK, delinquency findings in the A/OPC monthly review (22.a) and audit findings.

quantified_impact.metric: Difference between the two deadlines for the same trigger

risks.severity_reason: The conflict applies to every statement every month, so it is likely to cause confusion. The impact is mostly late certification rather than loss of funds.

risks.process: Reconcile and certify the monthly statement
risks.what_could_go_wrong: The CH's certified statement package with receipts sits with the AO/CO, or comes back to the CH, with no one tracking where it is. As a result, certification misses its deadline or documents are lost.
risks.cause: Section 10 says the CH 'will certify the bank statement and forward all documentation to the AO/CO', and Section 10.b(7) has the AO/CO 'return all supporting documentation to the CH'. No tracking, method or reminder is defined for either transfer.
risks.impact: Late certification and late payment. Missing support documents at audit time, which weakens the AO/CO certification the CO is pecuniarily liable for (3.d).

quantified_impact.metric: Handoffs of the documentation package per statement
quantified_impact.basis: Handoffs after S53 (CH to AO/CO) and S58 (AO/CO to CH)

quantified_impact.value: 5 business days, 10 business days, 15 calendar days

risks.severity_reason: The handoff happens monthly for every cardholder and has three deadlines riding on it. Lost documentation directly undermines certification liability.

risks.what_could_go_wrong: The cardholder types each transaction into the NETC 4430/1 log and later compares it line by line with the CitiDirect statement. Typing errors or missed entries create false mismatches or hide real ones.
risks.cause: Section 7.e requires every transaction to be recorded in the purchase card log. Section 10.a requires the CH to verify each statement transaction against the log and LOA. The log is 'manual or automated' (2.l), so the same data is held in two places.
risks.impact: Reconciliation takes longer. Errors can lead to wrong LOA charges or undetected improper charges, which affects certification accuracy.

quantified_impact.metric: Places the same transaction data is recorded

risks.severity_reason: This happens on every transaction. Each error is usually caught at reconciliation but costs time and can mis-charge funds.

risks.what_could_go_wrong: The cardholder certifies the quality and quantity of items they bought themselves, so the same person both places the order and confirms receipt. This defeats the required separation of function.
risks.cause: Section 7.d(2) tells the cardholder to 'Certify that the quality and quantity of the items furnished are per this agreement'. Section 9.a says 'The CH shall not initiate the requirement, award the purchase action, and receive, inspect, and accept' and requires a different person for receipt/inspection and for acceptance.
risks.impact: Separation-of-duties control weakens, which creates audit findings and fraud exposure. The AO may rely on a certification the SOP elsewhere forbids the CH to make.
risks.severity_reason: The conflict applies to every received order. Its impact is a control weakness rather than a direct loss.

risks.what_could_go_wrong: N4 approves a purchase above the cardholder's single purchase limit, but CITIBANK's authorization system still declines the card at checkout because nobody raised the limit at the bank.
risks.cause: Section 8 allows the single purchase limit to be exceeded 'if approved by N4'. Section 19 says CITIBANK checks the single purchase limit before authorizing. Only the A/OPC submits limit changes to CITIBANK (3.b). No step connects the N4 approval to a limit change.
risks.impact: The purchase is delayed, the cardholder has to call the A/OPC (S40), and the merchant order may be lost.

quantified_impact.metric: Steps defined between N4 approval and bank limit change
quantified_impact.basis: Sections 8, 19 and 3.b; no such step in map

risks.severity_reason: This occurs only for over-limit purchases. When it does occur, the purchase is very likely blocked.

risks.what_could_go_wrong: A purchase request is stopped because funds are not committed, the AO does not approve, the price is not fair and reasonable, the item is on the restricted list, or the bank denies it. The requester never learns what happens next.
risks.cause: Decision D7 (funds, 6.a/7.a(2)), the AO-disapproval exception at S33 (7.a(3)) and D10 (price, 7.b) have no stated next step. Section 12 lists restricted items with no alternative route. Section 19 has the CH contact the A/OPC for denials with no resolution step.
risks.impact: Requests stall without a record of the reason. Requesters may resubmit through other channels, and workarounds can bypass controls.

quantified_impact.metric: Undefined branches or exceptions in this process
quantified_impact.value: 5 (D7 No, S33 disapproval, D10 No, Section 12 restricted item, S40 denial)
quantified_impact.basis: Counted from decisions and exceptions in map

risks.severity_reason: At least one of these branches is likely to occur regularly. The impact is delay and an untracked outcome rather than loss.

risks.what_could_go_wrong: Signed SF 182 copies are sent separately to N4, HRO, N8 and the cardholder, and one copy is late or missed. The cardholder does not know the training can be paid, or HRO receives the form before N4.
risks.cause: Section 16.c makes the division contact N4 for CH information. Section 16.d requires a copy to N4 'prior to forwarding to Human Resources Office'. Section 6.b requires signed copies to N8 and the CH. All of these are manual distributions with no tracking.
risks.impact: Training registration is delayed or missed, payment is made without N4's record, and the ordering rule in 16.d is breached.

quantified_impact.basis: Handoffs after S12, S14, S15 and S16 (x2) in map

risks.severity_reason: This occurs for every training request and involves several manual copies. Usually only delay results.

risks.what_could_go_wrong: A division prepares an SF 182 for training above $25,000 or not off-the-shelf, and nobody tells them how the training should be bought instead.
risks.cause: Section 16.b says 'The GCPC may not be used to pay for training in excess of $25,000 when using SF 182', and 16.a sets eligibility. Neither section gives an alternative route. Decision D3 'No' leads to UNDEFINED.
risks.impact: Training is delayed, or there is a risk the purchase is split or improperly paid by card.
risks.severity_reason: Few training requests exceed the threshold. The impact is delay, plus some compliance exposure if the request is split.

risks.what_could_go_wrong: A funding request emailed to N8, or the LOA and document number emailed back, gets buried in an inbox. The cardholder never receives a clear request to buy.
risks.cause: Section 6.c says 'Requests are emailed to N8' and the LOA and document number are 'provided to the requestor, and to the purchase card holder'. Section 6.d has signed copies provided to N8 and the CH. No tracking or status is defined.
risks.impact: Requirements are delayed, requesters chase N8, and there is no record of what was funded when.

quantified_impact.basis: Handoffs after S17, S22 (x2) and S24 (x2) in map

risks.severity_reason: This affects every centrally managed request. Email is untracked, but the impact is mainly delay.

risks.what_could_go_wrong: An unusual request reviewed by the Comptroller or Legal, or a requirement sent to the Comptroller because funds ran out, gets a decision that never returns to N8 or the requestor.
risks.cause: Section 6.c says unusual requests are forwarded 'for review prior to taking action', and Section 6.e says exhausted-funding requirements are 'forwarded to the Comptroller for review'. Neither section states the outcome path.
risks.impact: Requirements sit indefinitely, the requestor is not told, and needed purchases are delayed or never made.

quantified_impact.basis: Exceptions at S19 and S25 in map

risks.severity_reason: This is likely whenever funds run short or a request is unusual. The impact is an open-ended delay.

risks.what_could_go_wrong: No one tracks when each participant's two-year refresher, annual ethics or annual CLG 006 training is due. A cardholder or AO is suspended without warning, or keeps using the card while out of compliance.
risks.cause: Section 5.b says failure 'will result in suspension of account' but names no one to suspend it. Certificates go to the A/OPC (5.c(2)), but no tracking or reminder duty is assigned. Sections 5.c and 5.d add annual requirements.
risks.impact: Purchasing stops unexpectedly for a suspended cardholder, or non-compliant participants keep transacting, which becomes an audit finding.

quantified_impact.value: 2 (DoD ethics; CLG 006 for COs and D/AOs)

risks.severity_reason: Recurring deadlines with no tracking are likely to be missed. The consequence is account suspension or a compliance finding.

risks.what_could_go_wrong: The A/OPC is out when a cardholder reports fraud, a lost card or a denied transaction. The bank is not contacted 'immediately' and there is no named backup.
risks.cause: Section 3.b states 'The GCPC Program Manager (N4), 850-452-3996, performs the A/OPC function'. Sections 11, 11.b(1), 17.b, 19 and 20 route time-critical work to the A/OPC. No alternate is named anywhere.
risks.impact: Fraudulent charges continue, account closure and replacement are delayed, and departures or denials go unhandled.

quantified_impact.metric: Mapped steps where the A/OPC is the actor

quantified_impact.basis: Handoffs after S1, S3, S10, S40, S51, S56, S62, S70, S78, S79, S81

risks.severity_reason: A single role sits on many time-critical paths, including the 'immediately' fraud notice. Absence is likely over a year, and the financial impact is direct.

risks.what_could_go_wrong: A suspect transaction is reported as both a dispute and fraud. The invoice is short-paid twice and the account becomes delinquent.
risks.cause: Section 11 warns that using both procedures 'may cause payments to be incorrectly short-paid and the account will become delinquent'. The only control is that the CH or AO 'must contact the A/OPC', with no record of the determination.
risks.impact: The account becomes delinquent and payment is wrong. Manual clean-up is needed with CITIBANK.

quantified_impact.basis: Steps S62-S63 have no recorded output

risks.severity_reason: This is unlikely if the A/OPC is consulted, but the SOP itself names a delinquency consequence.

risks.what_could_go_wrong: The cardholder disputes a charge in CitiDirect but the signed paper dispute form is not faxed, is faxed with different details, or is faxed late. CITIBANK then cannot act within the 60-day window.
risks.cause: Section 11.a(2) requires the electronic dispute to be 'backed up by faxing or mailing the form to CITIBANK' because the bank needs the CH signature. Section 11.a(5) sets a 60-day limit. Tracking in 11.a(3) is by phone or log review with no reminder.
risks.impact: The dispute is lost and the charge must be paid. Unresolved short-pays cause account balance problems.

quantified_impact.metric: Times the same dispute is submitted

risks.severity_reason: Duplicate submission on every dispute makes a miss reasonably likely. A missed deadline means paying a disputed charge.

risks.process: Reconcile and certify the monthly statement
risks.what_could_go_wrong: The AO/CO reports a suspected unauthorized purchase, or a charge is found to be misuse that cannot be disputed. Nothing defines whether certification is held, who investigates, or how the charge is resolved.
risks.cause: Section 10.b(4) only says 'Notify the A/OPC or NETC N4'. Section 11.a says misuse or abuse 'are not disputable' with no alternative (decision D22 leads to UNDEFINED). Section 13.b puts investigation with the supervisor, but no section links the AO's notice to the supervisor.
risks.impact: A suspect charge may be certified for payment, misuse cases go uninvestigated, and the CO bears pecuniary liability (3.d).

quantified_impact.metric: Branches or steps with no next step

risks.severity_reason: This is uncommon, but when it occurs it involves possible fraud or misuse with money and liability at stake.

risks.process: Reconcile and certify the monthly statement
risks.what_could_go_wrong: When the cardholder is away, the AO reviews and certifies the statement alone. Because the AO and CO are the same person, no second set of eyes checks the transactions until the CH returns, possibly after payment.
risks.cause: Section 10.a(3) has the AO review and certify when the CH is unavailable and 'meet with the CH upon their return', with no timing. Sections 3.c and 3.d state 'The same person performs the roles of AO and CO'.
risks.impact: Errors or improper charges are paid without cardholder verification, which becomes an audit finding.

quantified_impact.metric: People reviewing before certification when CH is absent

risks.severity_reason: CH absences at statement time are fairly common, and payment proceeds without the normal two-party check.

risks.process: Report a lost or stolen card
risks.what_could_go_wrong: The cardholder tells the AO about a lost card, but the AO's written report to the A/OPC is late or missing details such as same-day purchases. The A/OPC cannot confirm what to block or dispute.
risks.cause: Section 17.b requires the CH to notify the AO and A/OPC within one business day, then the AO to submit a separate written report with seven data items within one business day. The data is passed twice by hand.
risks.impact: Fraudulent use of the lost card may go unchallenged, and the deadlines in 17.b are missed.

quantified_impact.value: 1 business day (CH notice) and 1 business day (AO report)

quantified_impact.metric: Data items re-entered in AO report

risks.severity_reason: This is rare, but tight deadlines and duplicated data make delay likely when it happens.

risks.what_could_go_wrong: A cardholder transfers or retires without the A/OPC finding out in time, and the card stays active after departure.
risks.cause: Section 20 requires the account to be inactive 30 days before departure 'to the maximum extent possible' and limits reduced 'as soon as practical'. No step tells the A/OPC that a cardholder is leaving.
risks.impact: An active card held by a departed employee creates fraud exposure and breaches Section 20's rule that accounts 'shall not remain active past their official departure'.

quantified_impact.basis: Map (S82 input 'Notice of CH departure' has no source step)

risks.severity_reason: There is no trigger, so a late discovery is likely. The exposure is an uncontrolled active card.

risks.what_could_go_wrong: A departing cardholder's paper transaction files are incomplete or misplaced when turned in. Documents cannot be found during the 10-year retention period when auditors ask.
risks.cause: Section 21 requires all files to be 'turned in to the AO/CO for retention when a CH leaves'. It also requires financial records to be retained for 10 years. No index, check or storage method is defined.
risks.impact: There are audit findings for missing support, and certifications cannot be defended.
risks.severity_reason: Paper files changing hands at departure are often incomplete. The impact surfaces at audit.

risks.what_could_go_wrong: The semi-annual program review is prepared and approved by the same office, so weaknesses in the A/OPC's own oversight are not independently challenged. If approval is refused, no path is defined.
risks.cause: Section 3.a states 'The HA responsibilities have been delegated to N4', and Section 3.b states the GCPC Program Manager (N4) performs the A/OPC function. Section 22.b has the A/OPC provide the report to the HA (N4) for approval. Decision D26 'No' leads to UNDEFINED.
risks.impact: Control weaknesses reach CCPMD unchallenged, which could contribute to a failed PMR review (23.b).

quantified_impact.metric: Offices holding both preparer and approver roles

risks.severity_reason: The structural overlap exists every cycle. The impact is weaker oversight rather than direct loss.

risks.what_could_go_wrong: No one owns forwarding the review package by a known date, or running the suspension and stand-down training after a failed review. The package is late or the corrective actions stall.
risks.cause: Section 23.a says the review 'will be forwarded by traceable means to the PMR Team by the required date' without naming the actor or date. Section 23.b states the suspension and training 'will' occur without naming who does them.
risks.impact: The package is late to the PMR Team, and the post-failure actions are disorganized, delaying the 180-day follow-up.
risks.severity_reason: This occurs once every 18 months. The impact is mainly delay.

risks.what_could_go_wrong: The receipt/inspection and acceptance signatures are missing, illegible or come from the cardholder. The AO only finds out when initialing receipts at month end, after the money has been charged.
risks.cause: Section 9.a requires separate people to receive/inspect and accept 'by legible signature and date' on paper. Section 10.b(5) has the AO verify this by 'placing initials in a corner of each of the CH's transaction receipts'.
risks.impact: Payment is certified without proof of receipt, separation of duties is breached, and audit findings follow.
risks.severity_reason: Paper signatures on every order are prone to gaps. The check happens only after the charge.

risks.what_could_go_wrong: The sponsoring department forgets to send N4 the final conference bill, or sends the approval request after commitments are made, so N4 cannot match charges to the LOA.
risks.cause: Section 15.a gives no timing for the approval request copy. Section 15.b says only 'upon completion of the conference', with no deadline or reminder.
risks.impact: Conference charges cannot be matched to funding at reconciliation, causing delays and possible mis-charges.
risks.severity_reason: Conferences are infrequent. The impact is reconciliation delay.

risks.what_could_go_wrong: Year-end unfunded requirements are collected through untracked replies. A cardholder buys an item N8 did not approve, or an approved item is missed before funds lapse.
risks.cause: Section 6.f says N8 'notifies the Division Directors/Special Assistants' and departments are notified once funding is identified. Cardholders 'will only make end-of-fiscal-year purchases that have been approved by N8', but no approval record is defined.
risks.impact: Unapproved purchases may be made, or year-end funds lapse.
risks.severity_reason: This happens once a year with time pressure. The impact is limited to year-end purchases.

risks.process: Reconcile and certify the monthly statement
risks.what_could_go_wrong: A paid-but-not-received item or a promised warranty credit is forgotten after the cardholder pays in full. The next billing cycle passes and the dispute window closes.
risks.cause: Section 10.a(1) says the CH 'will track the transactions that have not been received', and 10.a(2) uses a paper 'suspense file'. Neither defines a reminder at the next billing cycle, and the 60-day dispute limit in 11.a(5) runs in parallel.
risks.impact: The government pays for goods never received, or credits are never collected.
risks.severity_reason: Manual tracking of open items is easy to forget. The government pays for goods it never received.

risks.what_could_go_wrong: The AO and cardholder identify an item as accountable property but never tell N4. The item is not recorded in DPAS and cannot be tracked.
risks.cause: Section 14.a has 'AOs and CHs identify' accountable property, while 14.b says 'DPAS is maintained by N4'. No handoff or timing is defined between them.
risks.impact: Sensitive or pilferable items are lost or stolen without a record, which becomes a property accountability finding.
risks.severity_reason: An untracked handoff for higher-value or pilferable items creates real theft exposure.

recommendations.label: digitize
recommendations.proposed_change: The requesting department submits the nomination in a Power Apps form that creates a record in a SharePoint GCPC Participant Register. The A/OPC and the nominee are notified automatically.
recommendations.reason: Section 4.a allows email or memo with no record. A register becomes the single source for training dates, limits, AO assignment and departure dates used by later flows.
implementation_steps: Create a SharePoint list 'GCPC Participant Register' with columns for name, role (CH/AO/CO), department, AO, nomination date, training dates, appointment date, limits, SF 1402 required, and departure date.
Build a Power Apps canvas form for nominations writing to the list.
Add a Power Automate flow on item creation that emails the A/OPC group mailbox and the nominee with the required initial training list from Section 5.a.

impact.basis: Replaces email or memo and the separate A/OPC notification (S1, 4.a) with one form entry. Minutes are an estimate.

recommendations.label: automate
recommendations.proposed_change: The nominee uploads certificates to their register record. A flow checks that every required course for the role is present and then notifies the HA or designee that the nominee is ready for appointment.
recommendations.reason: Section 5.a gates appointment on five courses (CLG 006 only for COs and D/AOs). An automatic completeness check removes manual review by the A/OPC.
implementation_steps: Add a SharePoint document library 'Training Certificates' with metadata for participant, course and completion date.
Create a flow triggered on file upload that updates course completion dates on the register item.
Add a condition that checks all role-specific courses are complete and then emails the HA/designee (N4) with a link to the record.

impact.basis: Removes the manual tally of certificates by the A/OPC (S3, 5.c(2)). Minutes are an estimate.

recommendations.label: keep_human
recommendations.proposed_change: The HA or designee continues to sign the delegation of authority and the SF 1402 Certificate of Appointment personally.
recommendations.reason: Delegating procurement authority and setting spending limits is a legal appointment decision (4.a, 4.b, 8) and must stay with an accountable official.
implementation_steps: Keep signature with the HA or designee.
Store the signed letter and SF 1402 on the participant's register record for reference by later flows.

impact.basis: No change to the step.

recommendations.label: automate
recommendations.proposed_change: A scheduled flow calculates each participant's two-year refresher and annual ethics and CLG 006 due dates from the register. It sends reminders before each due date and flags overdue participants to the A/OPC for suspension. Uploaded certificates reset the due dates automatically.
recommendations.reason: Section 5.b sets a two-year cycle with suspension but no tracker or owner. Sections 5.c and 5.d add annual requirements.
implementation_steps: Add due-date calculated columns (last refresher plus 2 years; last ethics plus 1 year; last CLG 006 plus 1 year) to the register.
Create a daily scheduled flow that filters items due in 60 or 30 days and emails the participant and their AO.
Have the same flow assign an A/OPC task in Planner or Teams, titled 'Suspend account per 5.b', for items past due.
Reuse the certificate-upload flow from A2 to update dates and close the suspension task when the certificate arrives.

impact.basis: Replaces manual tracking of due dates and manual certificate filing (S10, S11). Minutes are an estimate.

recommendations.label: digitize
recommendations.proposed_change: The division completes an SF 182 request in Power Apps. The form looks up the cardholder from the register instead of calling N4, pre-fills the Section C payment statement, and blocks or flags requests over $25,000 or not off-the-shelf.
recommendations.reason: Section 16.c requires contacting N4 for CH information. Sections 16.a and 16.b set eligibility with no alternative route, which the form can enforce.
implementation_steps: Create a SharePoint list 'SF 182 Requests' with LOA, cost, training type, employee and CH fields.
Build a Power Apps form with a lookup to the Participant Register for the CH name and phone.

Add validation that stops submission when cost exceeds $25,000 or the training is not off-the-shelf, and routes the request to N4 with a 'needs alternate contract route' status for the process owner to define.
Generate the SF 182 PDF from a Word template using the Word Online (Business) connector.

impact.basis: Removes the Division-to-N4 lookup handoff after S12 and the manual entry of CH and Section C text. Minutes are an estimate.

recommendations.label: automate
recommendations.proposed_change: An approval flow collects the required signatures. It then distributes the signed SF 182 to N4 first, forwards it to HRO only after N4's copy is logged, and notifies N8 and the cardholder that the purchase can be made.
recommendations.reason: Four separate manual distributions with an ordering rule (16.d) are rule-based and easy to automate.
implementation_steps: Trigger the flow on a new SF 182 Requests item.
Use 'Start and wait for an approval' (sequential) for the department signers, then save the approval history on the item.
On approval, email the PDF to the N4 mailbox and record the date sent.
Then email HRO, N8 and the assigned CH, and set status to 'Ready to purchase'.

impact.basis: Replaces 4 manual copy distributions (handoffs after S14, S15, S16 x2) with automated sends. Wait days and minutes are estimates.

recommendations.label: digitize
recommendations.proposed_change: Requestors submit centrally managed requirements in a Power Apps form to a SharePoint Funding Requests list with visible status, replacing email to N8.
recommendations.reason: Section 6.c relies on email with no tracking of the request or its review outcome.
implementation_steps: Create a SharePoint list 'Funding Requests' with requirement, amount, category, documentation required (SF 182 or NETC 4235/4), status, LOA and document number.
Build a Power Apps form for requestors and an N8 view filtered by status.
Show status to requestors (Submitted, Under review, Funded, Sent to Comptroller, Returned).

impact.basis: The email request becomes a tracked list item (S17). Minutes are an estimate of time saved on status follow-up.

recommendations.label: ai_assist
recommendations.proposed_change: An AI step reads each new request description and flags likely unusual or questionable items, such as Section 12 restricted categories, travel, telecom or HAZMAT, for N8. N8 still decides whether to forward the request.
recommendations.reason: Section 6.c leaves 'unusual or questionable' to judgment. A text classifier gives N8 a consistent first screen.
implementation_steps: Add a flow step on new Funding Requests that calls an AI Builder prompt (or custom classification model) with the request text and the Section 12 restricted list.
Write the AI flag and rationale to columns on the item.
Notify N8 when the flag is set, and have N8 choose 'Forward to Comptroller/Legal' or 'Routine'.
recommendations.suggested_tool: AI Builder prompt in Power Automate

impact.basis: Estimate of N8 reading time saved. The decision stays with N8.

recommendations.label: keep_human
recommendations.proposed_change: The Deputy Comptroller, Comptroller and Legal (N00D) continue to review unusual or questionable requests themselves.
recommendations.reason: Legal and fiscal judgment on unusual requirements (6.c) must stay with accountable officials.
implementation_steps: Keep the review human.
Record the review outcome on the Funding Requests item so N8 and the requestor see it.

impact.basis: No change to the step.

recommendations.label: automate
recommendations.proposed_change: When N8 enters the LOA and document number, a flow sends them to the requestor and the cardholder with the purchase request. When the requestor uploads signed documentation, the flow sends it to N8 and the cardholder.
recommendations.reason: Both distributions are rule-based copies of data already in the list (6.c, 6.d).
implementation_steps: Trigger on Funding Requests item modified, with LOA and document number filled and status set to Funded.
Email the requestor and CH with the LOA, document number and a link to the item.
Add a second trigger on attachment of the signed SF 182 or NETC 4235/4 that emails N8 and the CH and sets status to 'Ready to purchase'.

impact.basis: Automates the handoffs after S22 (x2) and S24 (x2) and removes the retyping of LOA and document number into emails. Wait days and minutes are estimates.

recommendations.label: automate
recommendations.proposed_change: When N8 marks a requirement 'Funding exhausted', a flow sends it to the Comptroller as an approval with outcomes (fund, defer, deny). It writes the outcome back to the request and notifies the requestor.
recommendations.reason: Section 6.e gives no outcome path after Comptroller review. An approval with recorded outcomes closes the loop; the process owner must confirm the outcome options.
implementation_steps: Trigger on status changed to 'Funding exhausted'.
Run 'Start and wait for an approval' with custom responses (Fund, Defer, Deny) assigned to the Comptroller.
Update status and comments on the item and email the requestor and N8.
Escalate to the Deputy Comptroller if there is no response in 5 business days (process owner to confirm the timeframe).

impact.basis: Adds a defined outcome and notification to S25. Minutes are an estimate of follow-up time.

recommendations.label: digitize
recommendations.proposed_change: N8 sends a Microsoft Form to Division Directors and Special Assistants, and responses land in one list. N8 marks each requirement approved so cardholders can see exactly which end-of-year buys are authorized.
recommendations.reason: Section 6.f requires N8 approval before any end-of-year purchase, but the request and response are untracked.
implementation_steps: Create a Microsoft Form for unfunded requirements (item, amount, priority, department).
Use a flow to copy each response into a SharePoint list 'EOFY Requirements'.
Add an 'N8 Approved' column and a view for cardholders that shows only approved items.

impact.basis: Replaces email collection and consolidation by N8 (S26, S27). Minutes are an estimate.

recommendations.label: digitize
recommendations.proposed_change: The cardholder starts every purchase in a Power Apps purchase request form. The form captures the LOA and funds confirmation, the mandatory-source screening, and a Section 12 restricted-item check. Stopped requests get a recorded reason and the requester is notified.
recommendations.reason: Funds and screening checks (6.a, 7.a) are undocumented today, and stopped requests have no defined outcome.
implementation_steps: Create a SharePoint list 'GCPC Purchase Requests' with requester, item, amount, LOA, funds confirmed, mandatory source checked, restricted category, status and stop reason.
Build a Power Apps form with required fields and a dropdown of Section 12 categories that blocks submission for restricted items.
Pull the CH's single purchase limit from the Participant Register so the form can flag over-limit amounts.
Notify the requester of any 'Stopped' status with the reason.

impact.basis: Documents S30 and S31 in one entry that later steps reuse. Minutes are an estimate.

recommendations.label: automate
recommendations.proposed_change: A flow routes each purchase request to the AO for approval, and first to N4 if it exceeds the single purchase limit. After N4 approval it tells the A/OPC to submit the limit change to CITIBANK. Approval or disapproval is recorded and the cardholder is notified.
recommendations.reason: AO approval before purchasing (7.a(3)) and N4 approval over the limit (8) are rule-based routings. Linking them to the bank limit change (3.b, 19) closes an undefined gap.
implementation_steps: Trigger when a GCPC Purchase Requests item is created with status 'Submitted'.
Get the CH's limits from the Participant Register and compare them with the amount.
If over the single purchase limit, run 'Start and wait for an approval' assigned to N4. On approval, create a task for the A/OPC to submit a limit change to CITIBANK.
Run 'Start and wait for an approval' assigned to the CH's AO, then write the outcome and comments to the item.
Email the CH on 'AO Approved' or 'Stopped - AO disapproved' with comments.

impact.basis: Handoffs after S31, S32 and S33 remain but become tracked approvals. Wait days and minutes are estimates.

recommendations.label: digitize
recommendations.proposed_change: The paper or spreadsheet NETC 4430/1 purchase card log becomes a SharePoint list. Each entry is created automatically from the approved purchase request, so the cardholder only adds the transaction date, final amount and receipt.
recommendations.reason: Section 7.e requires every transaction logged with its audit trail. The request already holds most of the data, so re-entry is avoidable.
implementation_steps: Create a SharePoint list 'Purchase Card Log' with the NETC 4430/1 fields plus a link to the purchase request and approval history.
Create a flow on request status 'AO Approved' that creates the log item with copied fields.
Ask the CH, through a Teams adaptive card or Power Apps, to add the transaction date, amount and receipt attachment.
Export the log view as NETC 4430/1 for the monthly statement package.

impact.basis: Removes retyping the request details into the log (S41). Minutes are an estimate.

recommendations.label: digitize
recommendations.proposed_change: The receiver/inspector and the acceptor record receipt and acceptance in a Power Apps screen tied to the log entry. Each record captures the signer's identity and date, and the app blocks the cardholder or ordering person from signing either role.
recommendations.reason: Section 9.a requires three different people with legible signature and date. A digital record enforces separation and gives the AO proof without initialing paper.
implementation_steps: Add receipt/inspection and acceptance columns (person, date, quantity received, notes) to the Purchase Card Log.
Build a Power Apps screen that uses the signed-in user for each role.
Add a validation rule that rejects the entry if the user is the CH or the award person, with an emergent-situation override that enforces only the two-way rule from 9.b and records a justification.

impact.basis: Replaces paper signatures on S42 and S43 with recorded identity. Minutes are an estimate.

recommendations.label: eliminate
recommendations.proposed_change: Remove the cardholder's separate quality and quantity certification. The independent acceptance in S43 already certifies that the delivered items match the order. The process owner should confirm this reading of 7.d(2) against 9.a.
recommendations.reason: The CH certification duplicates acceptance and conflicts with the separation-of-function rule in Section 9.a.
implementation_steps: Confirm with the HA (N4) and the policy owner that acceptance under 9.a satisfies 7.d(2).
Remove the CH certification field from the log and IOP training materials.
Update the IOP text in the next revision.

impact.basis: Removes step S44. Minutes are an estimate.

recommendations.label: automate
recommendations.proposed_change: When a log entry is created, a flow checks the unit cost (at or above $5,000) and a pilferable or sensitive category flag. It notifies N4 with the item details to record in DPAS and tracks the task until N4 enters the DPAS number.
recommendations.reason: Section 14.a sets a clear rule-based threshold, but there is no handoff to N4, who maintains DPAS (14.b).
implementation_steps: Add unit cost and 'sensitive/pilferable/classified' columns to the Purchase Card Log.
Create a flow on item creation or modification with a condition of unit cost at or above 5000 or the flag set to Yes.
Assign a Planner task to N4 with the item details and a DPAS number field, and remind weekly until it is completed.

impact.basis: The handoff after S45 becomes tracked. Minutes are an estimate.

recommendations.process: Reconcile and certify the monthly statement
recommendations.label: automate
recommendations.proposed_change: At billing cycle end the cardholder uploads the CitiDirect statement export. A flow matches each statement line to Purchase Card Log entries by date, merchant and amount and flags unmatched or LOA-mismatched lines for the cardholder to resolve.
recommendations.reason: Section 10.a requires line-by-line verification against the log. Matching is rule-based once both sets of data are digital. There is no standard CitiDirect connector, so the export is uploaded by hand.
implementation_steps: Create a document library 'Statements' where the CH uploads the CitiDirect CSV export.
Build a flow on file upload that parses the CSV (Excel Online table or Parse CSV action) and looks up log entries for the cycle.
Write match results to a 'Reconciliation Lines' list with status Matched, Unmatched or LOA mismatch.
Notify the CH with a link to the unmatched lines.

impact.basis: Replaces the manual comparison in S48. Minutes are an estimate and depend on the number of transactions.

recommendations.process: Reconcile and certify the monthly statement
recommendations.label: automate
recommendations.proposed_change: Pay-and-confirm and warranty items go into an open-items list with an expected-by date of the next billing cycle end. A flow reminds the cardholder before that date and, if the item or credit has not posted, starts the dispute intake or notifies the A/OPC, keeping the 60-day dispute limit in view.
recommendations.reason: Sections 10.a(1) and 10.a(2) rely on the cardholder's memory and a paper suspense file. The follow-up rules are clear and time-based.
implementation_steps: Create a SharePoint list 'Open Pay-and-Confirm Items' with transaction, type (not received or warranty), statement date, expected-by date and status.
Build a scheduled flow that emails the CH 5 days before the expected-by date and on the date itself.
If the status is not 'Received/Credited' after the expected-by date, create a dispute intake item (A26) for non-receipt, or email the A/OPC for an unposted warranty credit.
Add a 60-day-from-statement-date reminder column.

impact.basis: Replaces manual tracking in S49 and S50 and the manual notification in S51. Minutes are an estimate.

recommendations.process: Reconcile and certify the monthly statement
recommendations.label: digitize
recommendations.proposed_change: Explanations for missing documentation are entered in a form linked to the log entry, with every Section 10.c field required.
recommendations.reason: Section 10.c lists required content, which a form can enforce so incomplete explanations are not accepted.
implementation_steps: Add a 'Missing documentation explanation' screen in the Power Apps log app with required fields for item, cost, date, merchant, price, quantity and reason.
Save the explanation to the log item and flag it for AO review.

impact.basis: Estimate of time saved on rework of incomplete explanations.

recommendations.process: Reconcile and certify the monthly statement
recommendations.label: automate
recommendations.proposed_change: When the cardholder marks the cycle 'CH certified', a flow routes the digital package (statement, log, receipts, explanations) to the AO/CO. It shows both the 5- and 10-business-day due dates, sends reminders, and escalates to the A/OPC group before the deadline. Documents stay in SharePoint, so nothing is physically handed back.
recommendations.reason: The package handoff (Section 10) is untracked. The 5- versus 10-business-day conflict (10, 10.b(6)) needs both dates visible until the process owner sets one rule.
implementation_steps: Create a SharePoint list 'Monthly Reconciliations' with an item per CH per cycle, auto-created by a scheduled flow on the 20th, with the statement NEW date entered by the CH.
Calculate the 5- and 10-business-day due dates (using a holiday table) and a 15-calendar-day PAT due date.
On status 'CH certified', assign an approval to the AO/CO with links to the cycle's log view and documents.
Send reminders on business day 3 and escalate to the A/OPC group mailbox on business day 5 if the AO/CO step is incomplete.
Ask the process owner to confirm which deadline governs and update the flow.

impact.basis: The physical return of documents in S58 is no longer needed because files stay in SharePoint (1 handoff), and the S53 handoff becomes tracked. Wait days and minutes are estimates.

recommendations.process: Reconcile and certify the monthly statement
recommendations.label: ai_assist
recommendations.proposed_change: AI Builder receipt processing extracts merchant, date and amount from each attached receipt and compares them with the statement line. Mismatches or missing receipts are highlighted for the AO/CO, who still decides whether charges are appropriate.
recommendations.reason: The AO/CO must verify supporting documentation for all accounts (10.b(3)). Reading receipts is a good fit for AI extraction, especially when the AO reviews alone (10.a(3)).
implementation_steps: Add a flow on receipt upload that calls the AI Builder 'Extract information from receipts' prebuilt model.
Write the extracted fields to the log item and compare them with the reconciliation line amount and date.
Flag differences above a tolerance set by the process owner and show the flags in the AO/CO review view.
Keep the appropriateness judgment and certification with the AO/CO.
recommendations.suggested_tool: AI Builder receipt processing + Power Automate

impact.basis: Estimate of AO/CO receipt-reading time saved in S54.

recommendations.process: Reconcile and certify the monthly statement
recommendations.label: automate
recommendations.proposed_change: Instead of the AO initialing paper receipts, a flow checks that every transaction in the cycle has digital receipt/inspection and acceptance records from separate people. It lists any gaps for the AO/CO before certification.
recommendations.reason: Section 10.b(5) is a rule-based completeness check once A16 records exist.
implementation_steps: Add a flow step in the reconciliation routing that queries log items for the cycle.
Flag items missing receipt or acceptance records, or where signers match the CH.
Present the gap list in the AO/CO approval details and block the 'Ready to certify' status until gaps are cleared or explained.

impact.basis: Replaces manual initialing of each receipt (S55). Minutes are an estimate.

recommendations.process: Reconcile and certify the monthly statement
recommendations.label: keep_human
recommendations.proposed_change: The AO/CO continues to judge suspected unauthorized purchases, to certify the invoice in CitiDirect, and to review and certify when the cardholder is unavailable.
recommendations.reason: Certification carries personal pecuniary liability (3.d), and suspicion of misuse is a sensitive judgment about people.
implementation_steps: Keep these steps human.
Record the certification date on the Monthly Reconciliations item for tracking.

impact.basis: No change to the steps.

recommendations.label: digitize
recommendations.proposed_change: The cardholder or AO logs any suspect transaction in a Power Apps intake routed to an A/OPC group mailbox with a named backup. The A/OPC records the determination (dispute, fraud, or misuse not disputable). The list allows only one procedure per transaction ID, and misuse cases are routed to the supervisor.
recommendations.reason: Section 11 relies on an unrecorded phone call to prevent double reporting. A single A/OPC creates a bottleneck, and misuse cases have no next step.
implementation_steps: Create a SharePoint list 'Suspect Transactions' with transaction ID (enforce unique values), statement date, description, reporter, determination and status.
Build a Power Apps intake and send notifications to an A/OPC shared mailbox or Teams channel that includes a designated backup.
Add an A/OPC determination screen with the choices Dispute, Fraud, or Misuse (route to supervisor per 13.b).
Have a flow notify the CH of the determination and calculate the 60-day dispute deadline.

impact.basis: The handoffs after S62 and S63 become recorded. Minutes are an estimate.

recommendations.label: automate
recommendations.proposed_change: A flow fills the CITIBANK Appendix B dispute form from the intake record for the cardholder to sign. It records when the form is faxed or mailed, so data is not re-entered and proof of submission exists.
recommendations.reason: Section 11.a(2) requires a signed paper form duplicating the CitiDirect dispute.
implementation_steps: Create a Word template of Appendix B with content controls.
Use the Word Online (Business) 'Populate a Microsoft Word template' action from the Suspect Transactions item and convert it to PDF.
Send the PDF to the CH for signature (Adobe Sign or DocuSign connector, or wet signature), and capture the fax or mail date on the item.

impact.basis: Removes manual completion of Appendix B (S65). Minutes are an estimate.

recommendations.label: automate
recommendations.proposed_change: A scheduled flow reminds the cardholder to check the CitiDirect dispute log weekly until they record a resolution. It warns before the 60-day limit if the dispute or form has not been submitted.
recommendations.reason: Section 11.a(3) leaves tracking to phone calls or log checks with no reminders.
implementation_steps: Add status, CitiDirect dispute date and form sent date columns to Suspect Transactions.
Build a weekly scheduled flow that emails the CH for open disputes.
Send an alert at day 45 from the statement date if the dispute date or form sent date is empty.

impact.basis: Estimate of follow-up time saved in S66.

recommendations.label: digitize
recommendations.proposed_change: The cardholder reports suspected fraud through the Suspect Transactions intake marked 'Fraud - urgent'. This sends an immediate Teams and email alert to the A/OPC and a designated backup so CITIBANK can be called without delay.
recommendations.reason: Section 11.b(1) requires immediate notice to a single A/OPC with no backup.
implementation_steps: Add an urgent fraud option to the A26 intake app.
Create a flow that posts a Teams message and emails the A/OPC and backup.
Escalate to N4 leadership if the item is not acknowledged within 2 hours (process owner to confirm the timeframe).

impact.basis: The handoff after S70 is tracked and backed up. Minutes are an estimate.

recommendations.label: keep_human
recommendations.proposed_change: The A/OPC continues to call CITIBANK, and the AO/CO continues to short-pay and manually certify fraudulent invoices.
recommendations.reason: Fraud handling with the bank and manual certification of short-pays (11.b) involve legal and financial judgment.
implementation_steps: Keep these steps human.
Record the bank contact date and short-pay amount on the Suspect Transactions item.

impact.basis: No change to the steps.

recommendations.process: Report a lost or stolen card
recommendations.label: digitize
recommendations.proposed_change: After calling CITIBANK, the cardholder completes a lost-card form with the seven Section 17.b fields, which notifies the AO and the A/OPC group at once. The AO reviews and adds to the same record and submits it as the written report instead of retyping it.
recommendations.reason: Two manual notifications with one-business-day deadlines pass the same data twice.
implementation_steps: Create a SharePoint list 'Lost or Stolen Cards' with the seven required fields from 17.b(1)-(7).
Build a Power Apps form for the CH and a flow that emails the AO and A/OPC group on submission.
Assign the AO an approval to review and complete the record, with a reminder at 1 business day.
Record the replacement card received date and any found-card turn-in.

impact.basis: The separate CH-to-A/OPC notice is merged into one submission (1 handoff), and the AO no longer retypes the 7 fields. Wait days and minutes are estimates.

recommendations.label: automate
recommendations.proposed_change: Departure dates entered in the Participant Register trigger a flow 45 days ahead. It creates an A/OPC checklist (inactivate the account, collect files, reduce limits, close the account) and reminds the A/OPC until each item is done.
recommendations.reason: Section 20 requires the account to be inactive 30 days before departure, but no step tells the A/OPC someone is leaving.
implementation_steps: Require the AO or department to enter the planned departure date in the Participant Register (add it to the departure checklist given to supervisors).
Create a daily scheduled flow that finds departures within 45 days and creates a Planner checklist for the A/OPC.
Escalate to N4 if the account is not marked inactive by departure date minus 30 days.
Notify the CH and AO/CO to transfer files (A33).

impact.basis: Adds a trigger for S82 and tracking for S84 and S85. Minutes are an estimate.

recommendations.label: digitize
recommendations.proposed_change: Transaction files already live in SharePoint (log, receipts, reconciliations), so at departure the cardholder confirms completeness and ownership moves to the AO/CO. A 10-year retention label keeps the records for audit.
recommendations.reason: Section 21 requires turn-in on departure and 10-year retention, which paper files support poorly.
implementation_steps: Store all GCPC records in a SharePoint site with folders per CH.
Apply a Microsoft Purview retention label of 10 years to the libraries.
On departure, have a flow ask the CH to confirm completeness and reassign folder ownership to the AO/CO.

impact.basis: Removes physical file transfer and filing (S83, S86). Minutes are an estimate.

recommendations.label: digitize
recommendations.proposed_change: Departments submit the conference approval request with its LOA in a form to an N4 list. A flow reminds them to upload the final bill after the conference end date.
recommendations.reason: Section 15 has two untracked copies to N4 with no deadline for the final bill.
implementation_steps: Create a Microsoft Form or Power Apps form writing to a 'Conferences' list with LOA, dates and an approval attachment.
Add a flow that reminds the sponsor 5 days after the end date to upload the final bill, repeating weekly until it is uploaded.
Notify N4 on each upload.

impact.basis: Estimate of N4 chase time saved on S88.

recommendations.label: keep_human
recommendations.proposed_change: The supervisor continues to investigate suspected misuse and decide on corrective or disciplinary action.
recommendations.reason: Disciplinary decisions about people (13.b) must stay with a person.
implementation_steps: Keep this step human.
Route misuse determinations from the A26 intake to the supervisor by email for awareness.

impact.basis: No change to the step.

recommendations.label: automate
recommendations.proposed_change: The A/OPC uploads the semi-annual report, and a flow routes it for HA (N4) approval, recording who prepared it and who approved it. If the same person holds both roles, it flags this to the process owner. On approval it forwards the report to the Hierarchy Level 3 A/OPC; on rejection it returns the report with comments.
recommendations.reason: Routing and forwarding (22.b) are rule-based, and the record exposes the self-approval overlap from 3.a and 3.b.
implementation_steps: Create a library 'Semi-Annual Reviews' with preparer metadata.
Trigger on upload and run 'Start and wait for an approval' assigned to the HA (N4).
Add a condition: if the approver equals the preparer, email the process owner.
On approval, email the report to the Hierarchy Level 3 A/OPC. On rejection, return it to the A/OPC with comments.

impact.basis: Automates the handoffs after S92 and S94. Minutes are an estimate.

recommendations.label: keep_human
recommendations.proposed_change: The HA (N4) continues to review and approve the semi-annual report personally.
recommendations.reason: Approval of program oversight results is an accountable management judgment.
implementation_steps: Keep the step human, using the approval from A36.

impact.basis: No change to the step.

recommendations.label: digitize
recommendations.proposed_change: The A/OPC compiles the PMR package in a SharePoint library from a checklist of required documents with a named owner and due date. After HA approval, the A/OPC sends it by traceable means with the send date recorded.
recommendations.reason: Section 23.a leaves the forwarding actor and the 'required date' unstated.
implementation_steps: Create a SharePoint library 'PMR Review' with a checklist list of required documents, owners and the due date from the PMR letter.
Assign the A/OPC as the owner for forwarding and record the tracking number and send date.
Route the package to the HA through an approval before sending.

impact.basis: Estimate of compilation and tracking time saved in S97 and S99.

recommendations.label: keep_human
recommendations.proposed_change: The HA continues to review and approve the PMR package personally.
recommendations.reason: Approval of material submitted to an external auditor is an accountable management decision.
implementation_steps: Keep the step human.

impact.basis: No change to the step.

starter_flows.trigger: SharePoint: When an item is created in the 'GCPC Purchase Requests' list with Status = Submitted
actions: Get item from 'GCPC Participant Register' for the requesting CH (single purchase limit, AO).
Condition: Amount greater than single purchase limit.
If yes: Start and wait for an approval assigned to N4. If N4 rejects, update Status to 'Stopped - N4 disapproved', email the CH, and end.
If N4 approves: create a Planner task for the A/OPC group, 'Submit single purchase limit change to CITIBANK per 3.b', with the request link.
Start and wait for an approval assigned to the CH's AO, with request details and the screening answers.
Update the item with approver, date, outcome and comments.
If approved: set Status = 'AO Approved' (this triggers the A15 log flow) and email the CH. If rejected: set Status = 'Stopped - AO disapproved' and email the CH and requester with comments.
starter_flows.approval_step: N4 approval when the amount exceeds the single purchase limit (Section 8), followed by AO approval before purchasing (Section 7.a(3)).

starter_flows.trigger: SharePoint: When an item in 'Monthly Reconciliations' is modified and Status changes to 'CH certified'
actions: Get the cycle's statement NEW date from the item and calculate the 5-business-day and 10-business-day due dates (skipping weekends and dates in a 'Holidays' list) and the 15-calendar-day PAT due date from cycle end.
